html:
Senegal's national dish of rice cooked in a tomato sauce with fish and vegetables, said to come from Saint-Louis in the 19th century.

Its name in Wolof means rice and fish. It grew popular as the French shipped broken rice from Indochina to Senegal to feed the groundnut country, so families turned to rice instead of millet; the groundnut trade and imported rice changed how Senegal eats. UNESCO listed it as intangible cultural heritage in 2021. Variants are eaten across the region, and it has a rival claim to be the source of jollof rice.
sum: Senegal's national dish of rice cooked in a tomato sauce with fish and vegetables, said to come from Saint-Louis in the 19th century.
